study.question: Does the sign-sensitive benefit of the all-task transported Q pivot bit require fav participation in its source, or can the complementary cart+buy source recover it under external sign reversal?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: all-task negative/positive AUCs are 0.6689610675617089/0.6683760511656333 (negative-minus-positive 0.0005850163960756), while fav-only gives 0.6688025544975889/0.6687481637940922 (gap 0.0000543907034967). Removing fav from the negative bit source gave 0.6683238588338976, but its positive counterpart was never measured. Thus neither fav necessity for sign sensitivity nor aggregate-task complementarity is established. Provisional mechanism: aggregation of fav with cart/buy changes the nonlinear projected/reassigned Q pivot orientation in a way that matters more than either partition alone. Predict the complementary cart+buy source will fail to recover the all-task negative-sign advantage or full sign gap. This tests a source/sign interaction along training trajectories, not semantic correctness of the arbitrary sign or proof of interference.

Read cached primary benchmark section2.3 (39 lines); INFNet hub aggregation/broadcast and TokenFormer token interaction are forward representation alternatives. This study retains the incumbent and changes only its backward source/sign. These summaries are not full original-method audits.

study.proposed_difference: Complete a 2x2 source x sign contrast: cart+buy pivot-bit source (nuisance_line_fixed_angle_without_fav_bit) versus all-task source (nuisance_line_fixed_angle), each with reversed/ aligned external sign. No new helper or forward design; only select previously implemented source and sign branches. Recompute all helpers in every cell. All-task bridge cells replay the prior full expression exactly. Existing fav-only +/- outcomes provide a complementary partition comparison.
predictions: All-task bridge AUCs should reproduce 0.6689610675617089 (negative) and 0.6683760511656333 (positive) within a predeclared 1e-6 bridge tolerance; any larger discrepancy triggers an implementation/environment audit before attribution. This is a reproducibility gate, not a significance threshold.

The cart+buy negative cell should reproduce g3-r0061-fixed_angle_without_fav_bit_negative AUC0.6683238588338976 within the same tolerance; no rounding-independent mechanistic inference if it does not.

Primary directional prediction: D=(AUC_all_negative-AUC_all_positive)-(AUC_cartbuy_negative-AUC_cartbuy_positive)>0, and AUC_all_negative>AUC_cartbuy_negative. Report both raw contrasts even if the prediction fails.

At identical state/input/cotangents, source choices differ only by a global +/-1 multiplying the same canonical line; same support/radius, unchanged forward outputs/private gradients and exact external-sign antisymmetry precede the final cast. Default +1 for zero reduced Q introduces no new transfer gate.
Parameter counts and inference execution should remain identical; measure training overhead and quality/cost on host. No efficiency claim from unchanged capacity alone.
falsifiers: A cart+buy negative advantage and sign gap at least as large as all-task refutes the directional claim that fav participation is required for this trajectory effect. Similar full/fav/cartbuy outcomes leave aggregation specificity unsupported.
A weak or reversed D undermines the complementarity explanation even if one individual candidate wins click AUC.

Any source-dependent full-task gate/radius at fixed state, changed forward/private gradient, invalid masking, nonfinite backward or failed bridge rejects this implementation as an attribution control.

Absent independent seeds, uncertainty estimates and measured bit/geometry diagnostics, a positive D is provisional controlled evidence under one seed, not repeated mechanism support. No held-out conclusion is available.
